LAB: The Tools

01 — Branching design

articy:draft X

A third-act scene: three characters are forced to take a boat from an NPC. It has four endings, including a hidden branch that opens only if the player has told the truth and never been caught in a lie. Built as dialogue fragments, hubs, instructions and conditions over three global variables.

// Access restricted

The playable project file is available to the recruiters on request. The file stays off the public page because the flow contains the full branching structure and the story's resolution (narrative motives, endings, and script spoilers).

03 — Pipeline

One scene, four formats

This is the standard pipeline I use in my workflow. It includes four stages: the piece of prose taken from theMyst novel; the screenplay based on the canonical chain of events; the flow designed in articy:draft with alternative choices and outcomes; the JSON file that the game engine can read. The example of such a workflow is presented with the "Getting the Boat from Reggie" scene.

01 Prose (taken from the novel)

Reggie met them on the porch of the house in a leather jacket pulled on over bare skin. In his hand he held a bottle of beer, and from his broad, floating smile it could be concluded that this bottle was far from the first of the evening. Donal parked the Ford a few yards from the house, and when all three got out of the car, Reggie whistled in surprise:

"Wow, there's a whole lot of you! Buying that rusty tub by joint contribution or something? The boat's in the shed, already in the water, tank full, ready to go wherever you like this very minute." The young man pointed at the lopsided hut to the left of the house, took a substantial sip from the bottle and belched.

"Listen, Reggie," Ian pronounced, climbing onto the porch and wiping the raindrops from his face. "We can't buy the boat today, but we very much need to take it on rental."

Reggie hiccupped drunkenly and frowned:

"Hold on, mate... You said on the phone a buyer was coming right now. Is that him?" he nodded in Donal's direction.

"There is no buyer," Demme said impatiently. "We need your boat for a few hours; we'll pay you..."

"Go fuck yourself!" Reggie cut him off and spat angrily at the porch deck. "Pay the full price or get the hell out of my house!"

Ian glanced back at Donal and Saoirse, as though seeking their support. Donal answered his friend with a microscopic nod.

"I'm sorry, Reggie, but we're compelled to insist," Ian pronounced grimly, and drew the pistol from behind his belt.

"What the—" The young man's eyes went round with indignation when he saw the weapon aimed in his direction. "Do you have any idea what you're doing, asshole? You cretin, you don't even understand who you're messing with!"

In three strides Ian flew at Reggie, knocked the bottle out of his hand, and set the gun against his bare chest.

"I'm very sorry, but if you don't bring the keys now, I'll pull the trigger."

Reggie stared with wide eyes at Demme's contorted face, in which desperation and entreaty could be read. Donal took his place beside Ian and clicked open a switchblade, trying not to look at the stunned owner of the boat.

"I can't fucking believe it," Reggie said with bitterness, shoving his hands into his pockets. "Damn punks robbing me in my own house."

Donal cleared his throat and answered:

"We'll return the boat to you. We don't want her for free. It's just that right now you're the only person we can get one from."

Reggie drew a deep breath, turned on his heels, and opened the front door. Saoirse followed the men, keeping a step behind Donal.

INT./EXT. REGGIE'S PORCH — NIGHT

Rain. The Ford idles at the foot of the steps. REGGIE, mid-20s, comes out in a leather jacket over bare skin, a bottle of beer in his hand, buzzed and delighted about it.

REGGIE

Wow, there's a whole lot of you! Buying that rusty tub by joint contribution or something? The boat's in the shed, already in the water, tank full.

IAN

Listen, Reggie. We can't buy the boat today. We need to take her on rental for a few hours.

Reggie hiccups. The smile goes.

REGGIE

Hold on, mate... You said on the phone a buyer was coming right now. That him?

He nods at DONAL. Nobody answers.

REGGIE (CONT'D)

Then get the hell off my porch. Pay in full or get lost.

Ian looks back at Donal and SAOIRSE. Donal gives him a small nod.

IAN

I'm sorry, Reggie. We're compelled to insist.

He draws the pistol from behind his belt.

REGGIE

What the— Do you have any idea what you're doing, asshole? You cretin, you don't even understand who you're messing with.

Three strides. Ian knocks the bottle out of his hand — glass on the floor — and puts the muzzle against bare chest. Reggie reads his face and finds no bluff in it. Only desperation, and something close to begging.

IAN

I'm very sorry, but if you don't bring the keys now, I'll pull the trigger.

Donal takes his place at Ian's shoulder and clicks open a switchblade, trying not to look at the man he is helping to rob.

REGGIE

(hands into his pockets)

I can't fucking believe it. Damn punks, robbing me in my own house.

DONAL

We'll return the boat to you. We don't want her for free. It's just that right now you're the only person we can get one from.

Reggie looks at the crowd angrily, then turns and goes inside the house.

The gate that articy draws as a diamond is three words here:"requires": { "truthTold": true, "caught": false }. One project, two languages: one for the designers' tools, one for the game engine.

04 — Systemic dialogue

Bark system

Barks are the lines the player never chooses: the character speaks because the game state changed. Below is the set of triggers and rules that governs what protagonists and NPCs say under different circumstances.

// Rules

  • Suppression. Barks never fire during scripted dialogue or cutscenes.
  • Priority. One bark at a time. Higher priority cancels lower; equal priority drops the newcomer.
  • Shuffle bag. No line repeats until its pool is exhausted.
  • Cooldowns. Per category and per character, so the two protagonists never trade lines like a duet.
  • Stress narrowing. Under fire the pool drops to its shortest lines.
TriggerConditionPrioCooldownPoolSample line
combat · spottedfirst contact, per encounterhigh45s6"Damn it!" *cracks his knuckles*
combat · hurthealth < 30%high60s4*sigh of pain*
stealth · near-missdetection peaked, then fellmed30s5"Close... Too close."
explore · clue foundfirst inspection of this cluemed—unique"Honestly, I never thought we'd find anything here."
signal · proximitysignal rising AND fog presentlow90s8"It's gotten louder! Did you notice?"
idle40s no input, no threatlowest120s10"Why am I still here? What am I even doing alive?"
